LESSON: STANDING FIRM IN FAITH

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: The Church
Topic 5.3: Standing Firm in Faith

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Standing Firm in Faith. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why should you stand firm in your Christian faith?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. name the city where believers were first called Christians
2. retell how Stephen was stoned for standing firm in his faith
3. explain why they should not join ungodly groups

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: STANDING FIRM IN FAITH
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Standing Firm in Faith helps you succeed in CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: STANDING FIRM IN FAITH
Study Standing Firm in Faith like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Name the city where believers were first called Christians

What this means
In this part you learn to name the city where believers were first called Christians. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: name the city where believers were first called Christians.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Standing Firm in Faith” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can name the city where believers were first called Christians. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Retell how Stephen was stoned for standing firm in his faith

What this means
In this part you learn to retell how Stephen was stoned for standing firm in his faith. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: retell how Stephen was stoned for standing firm in his faith.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Standing Firm in Faith in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can retell how Stephen was stoned for standing firm in his faith. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Explain why they should not join ungodly groups

What this means
In this part you learn to explain why they should not join ungodly groups. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain why they should not join ungodly groups.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain why they should not join ungodly groups. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Standing Firm in Faith is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Standing Firm in Faith” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: name the city where believers were first called Christians)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Standing Firm in Faith in your own words. (skill: retell how Stephen was stoned for standing firm in his faith)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: explain why they should not join ungodly groups)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Standing Firm in Faith to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: name the city where believers were first called Christians.
3. Practise this skill: retell how Stephen was stoned for standing firm in his faith.
4. Practise this skill: explain why they should not join ungodly groups.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Standing Firm in Faith from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Standing Firm in Faith: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Standing Firm in Faith?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should you stand firm in your Christian faith?
2. Why should you not join ungodly groups?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Standing Firm in Faith means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: name the city where believers were first called Christians.
5. Be able to: retell how Stephen was stoned for standing firm in his faith.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
